Impeachment of
    Judges
Justice Yashwant Varma

Impeachment of Judges



• Recently, The Supreme Court dismissed Justice Yashwant
Varma’s plea challenging the impeachment inquiry committee.

• The Court refused to stall the inquiry, finding no illegality in the
panel’s constitution.

• The decision clears the way for the impeachment inquiry to
proceed.

Impeachment of Judges

What is impeachment?

• A judge may be removed from office through a motion adopted
by Parliament on grounds of proven misbehaviour or
incapacity.

• Impeachment, though not explicitly mentioned in the
Constitution, colloquially refers to the process by which a judge
can be removed from office by Parliament.

• The impeachment process for judges in India serves as a crucial
mechanism to uphold judicial accountability while preserving
the independence of the judiciary.

Impeachment of Judges


• Article 124(4) outlines the removal process for Supreme Court
judges, which is applicable to High Court judges as per Article
218, with grounds limited to proved misbehaviour and
incapacity.

• Proved misbehaviour refers to actions or conduct by a judge
that breaches ethical and professional standards of the judiciary.

• Incapacity refers to a judge's inability to perform judicial duties
due to physical or mental infirmity.

Impeachment of Judges


• A judge can be removed only by an order of the president,
based on a motion passed by both houses of Parliament.

• The procedure for removal of judges is elaborated in the Judges
Inquiry Act, 1968.

Impeachment of Judges

Process of impeachment –

• Under the Act, an impeachment motion may originate in either
house of Parliament.

• To initiate proceedings: (i) at least 100 members of Lok
Sabha may give a signed notice to the speaker, or (ii) at least
50 members of Rajya Sabha may give a signed notice to the
chairman.

• The speaker or chairman may consult individuals and examine
relevant material related to the notice, and may admit or refuse
the motion.

Impeachment of Judges


• If admitted, a three-member committee is formed, comprising
(i) a Supreme Court judge, (ii) the chief justice of a high
court, and (iii) a distinguished jurist.

• The committee frames charges, conducts an investigation, and
provides the judge an opportunity for a written defence.

• After investigation, the committee submits its report to the
speaker or chairman, who lays it before the house.

Impeachment of Judges


• If misbehaviour or incapacity is proven, the motion for removal
is debated and must be passed by (i) a majority of the total
membership and (ii) two-thirds of members present and
voting in that house.

• Once passed, the motion goes to the other house for adoption
with the same majority.

• If both houses adopt the motion, it is sent to the president, who
issues the order of removal.

Impeachment of Judges
Justice Varma’s case –

• The controversy began on March 14, 2025, when a fire broke out at Justice
Yashwant Varma’s Delhi residence, where fire personnel allegedly
discovered a large amount of cash.

• On July 21, 145 Lok Sabha members submitted an impeachment
motion to Speaker Om Birla under Articles 124, 217, and 218 of the
Constitution to remove Justice Varma.

• A three-judge in-house inquiry committee, constituted by then CJI
Sanjiv Khanna, included:
➢ Justice Sheel Nagu, Chief Justice of Punjab & Haryana HC,
➢ Justice G.S. Sandhawalia, Chief Justice of Himachal Pradesh HC,
➢ Justice Anu Sivaraman, judge of Karnataka HC.

Impeachment of Judges


• The committee confirmed that unaccounted cash was found
in the gutted storeroom at his residence after the March 14–15
blaze. CJI Khanna (retired) forwarded the report to the PM
and President in May after Justice Varma refused to resign.

• Justice Varma’s petition in the Supreme Court argues that the
in-house inquiry usurps Parliament’s exclusive powers under
Articles 124 and 218 to remove judges through an inquiry under
the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.

Impeachment of Judges


• Initial reports suggest close to ₹15 crore was found, though
the amount is not officially confirmed.

• The Supreme Court’s 25-page internal inquiry report,
included pictures and a video of the burnt currency notes
recovered from Justice Varma’s residence.

Impeachment of Judges

The proceedings so far –

• The in-house inquiry into allegations against Justice
Yashwant Varma was ordered by then Chief Justice of India
Sanjiv Khanna on March 22, 2025.

• The order followed a preliminary report submitted by D.K.
Upadhyaya, Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court, which
reported the discovery of substantial amounts of burnt
currency at Justice Varma’s residence during a fire on March
14, 2025.

Impeachment of Judges


• Justice Yashwant Varma, then of the Allahabad High
Court, filed a writ petition challenging the Supreme Court’s
in-house procedure, which formed the basis for adverse findings
against him in the currency recovery case.

• The in-house committee, comprising two High Court Chief
Justices and one High Court judge, confirmed the presence
and removal of cash from the residence.

• The matter reached the Supreme Court through two
separate legal challenges filed by Justice Varma in late
2025 and early 2026.

Impeachment of Judges


• In the first challenge (August 2025), Justice Varma
questioned the legality of the in-house inquiry initiated after the
March 2025 incident.

• He argued that the in-house mechanism was an “extra-
constitutional” process and that the public uploading of
photographs and videos of the recovered cash had prejudiced
his case.

• The in-house panel had concluded that Justice Varma
exercised “tacit or active control” over the recovered cash.

Impeachment of Judges


• On August 7, 2025, the Supreme Court dismissed his
petition, holding that the in-house procedure is a valid, legally
sanctioned “gap-filling mechanism” essential to maintaining
judicial purity and integrity.

• In the second challenge (January 2026), Justice Varma
approached the Supreme Court again, this time contesting the
parliamentary impeachment process initiated against him.

• After 158 Members of Parliament signed an impeachment
motion, the Lok Sabha Speaker constituted a three-member
inquiry committee under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.

Impeachment of Judges


• Justice Varma, filing the petition to conceal his identity,
challenged the Speaker’s unilateral decision to constitute the
committee.

• He argued that since impeachment notices were submitted in
both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha on July 21, 2025,
Section 3(2) of the Act made a Joint Committee mandatory.

• On January 16, 2026, the Supreme Court dismissed this
second petition, ruling that the Rajya Sabha notice had been
rejected at the threshold and was never admitted.

Impeachment of Judges

Major issues raised by justice Varma –

• He argued that the inquiry panel was formed in violation of
the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.

• A key contention was that an impeachment inquiry cannot be
initiated unless the motion is admitted simultaneously in
both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. He claimed that
action by only one House or its presiding officer was
procedurally invalid.

• Justice Varma alleged that the entire inquiry process was
premature and legally flawed.

Impeachment of Judges

What is the Supreme Court’s ruling?

• the Supreme Court refused to stall the inquiry and
dismissed the plea, filed by Justice Yashwant Varma
challenging the constitution of the impeachment inquiry
committee.

• The Court held that there was “no illegality” in the formation of
the parliamentary inquiry panel.

• Justice Varma had argued that the inquiry panel was invalid as
the impeachment motion was not admitted simultaneously in
both Houses of Parliament.

Impeachment of Judges


• The Supreme Court refused to interfere in the parliamentary
impeachment process, calling it premature.

• The decision allows the impeachment inquiry against a
sitting High Court judge to proceed, reinforcing judicial
accountability.

• It observed that the formation of an inquiry committee is
only a preliminary step and does not amount to removal of a
judge.

Impeachment of Judges


• The Court clearly distinguished between inquiry proceedings
and impeachment/removal, stating that inquiry is not
removal.

• The bench emphasized that the parliamentary impeachment
process should not be interfered with lightly by the judiciary.

• It ruled that the Speaker of the Lok Sabha acted within his
constitutional and statutory authority while constituting the
committee. The Court found no violation of constitutional
provisions or the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.
BMC Elections

BMC Elections



• Recently, The 2026 Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation
(BMC) elections marked a historic political shift in Mumbai’s
civic governance.

• Results declared on January 16–17, 2026 saw the BJP-led
Mahayuti alliance secure control of India’s richest civic body.

• The outcome ended over 25 years of dominance by the
Thackeray family in the BMC.

BMC Elections

BMC Elections –

• The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC),
previously referred to as the Bombay Municipal Corporation
from 1888 to 1995, serves as the governing civic authority of
Mumbai, the capital of Maharashtra.

• The BMC is the wealthiest municipal corporation in India, the civic
body’s budget for the 2025–26 financial year is over ₹74,000
crore, an annual budget larger than that of several smaller Indian
states.

BMC Elections


• It was formed under the Bombay Municipal Corporation Act
of 1888 during British India, the BMC manages Mumbai’s civic
services, infrastructure, and administration, including certain
suburban areas.

• The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation is led by an IAS
officer, designated as the Municipal Commissioner, who holds
the primary executive authority.

• In June 2008, BMC conducted all administrative work in Marathi,
causing controversy, later, forms in English were also accepted to
accommodate citizens.

BMC Elections

Making of BMC –

• The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), originally
the Bombay Municipal Corporation, is among India’s oldest
and wealthiest civic bodies, reflecting Mumbai’s transformation
from seven islands into a global commercial hub.

• In 1805, basic municipal administration began in an
unorganized manner.

• In 1807, civic governance was vested in a Court of Petty
Sessions, consisting of two magistrates and a Justice of the
Peace.

BMC Elections


• In 1845, a Board of Conservancy (Civic Heptarchy) was
established to manage municipal funds. In 1858, a three-
commissioner board was appointed but failed to significantly
improve sanitary conditions.

• In 1865, the Municipal Corporation was formally established as a
Body Corporate, with Sir Arthur Crawford appointed as the
first Municipal Commissioner.

• The Municipal Act of 1872, largely drafted by Sir
Pherozeshah Mehta (the “Father of Municipal Government
in Bombay”), created a regular corporation with 64 members.

BMC Elections


• The Municipal Corporation Act of 1888 streamlined civic
administration, defined representative responsibilities, and
continues as the primary governing law of the BMC, with later
amendments.

• In 1893, the iconic Gothic-style headquarters of the
corporation was completed opposite Victoria Terminus (now
Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus – CSMT).

• Between 1922 and 1931, voting rights were expanded from
only property tax-payers to include rent-payers, and in 1931
the head’s title changed from “President” to “Mayor”.
BMC Elections

BMC Elections


• Between 1947 and 1950, post-Independence territorial
expansion occurred, with suburbs merged in 1950 and
Extended Suburbs added in 1957.

• In 1952, the corporation became a fully elected body, ending
ex-officio and government-appointed memberships.

• In 1995, following the city’s renaming, the civic body was
officially renamed the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation
(BMC).

BMC Elections

• The 2026 BMC elections –

• The 2026 Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC)
  elections were held on January 15, 2026, marking a historic shift
  as the BJP-led Mahayuti alliance secured a clear majority.

• Mumbai followed a single-member ward system, with voting
  conducted using Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) across
  10,231 polling stations.

• The election saw the debut of 140 PADU machines, introduced to
  streamline voting and manage crowds more efficiently.

• Printing Auxiliary Display Unit developed by Bharat
  Electronics Ltd (BEL), Bengaluru.

BMC Elections


• The main contest was among three fronts: the Mahayuti Alliance
of BJP and Shiv Sena (Eknath Shinde), Maha Vikas Aghadi
(MVA) )—comprising Shiv Sena (UBT), MNS, and NCP (Sharad
Pawar), and the Congress Front consisting of the Indian
National Congress (INC) and Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi.

• Among other parties, AIMIM won 8 seats mainly in Muslim-
dominated wards, NCP (Ajit Pawar) won 3 seats, Samajwadi
Party won 2 seats, while AAP failed to win any seat.

BMC Elections

Results of recent BMC elections –

• The result for 227 wards in the BMC declared by the State
Election Commission following the polls on 15th Jan, which were
held after a four-year delay.

• The Bharatiya Janata Party-led Mahayuti alliance has taken a
comfortable lead in the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation
(BMC).

• The coalition was spearheaded overall by Devendra Fadnavis
(BJP) with significant alliance coordination and campaigning with
Eknath Shinde (Shiv Sena) in the 2026 BMC polls.

BMC Elections

• The opposition coalition was spearheaded overall by Uddhav Thackeray
(Shiv Sena–UBT), with significant alliance coordination and campaigning
alongside Raj Thackeray (Maharashtra Navnirman Sena) in the 2026
BMC polls.

• As per the SEC, the overall voter turnout for the BMC polls stood at 52.90%,
which over 54 lakh stepping out to vote.

• The last BMC elections were held in 2017. Based on the schedule, the
elections were set for 2022 but were delayed due to a series of factors. Among
the key reasons for the delay in elections was due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Other reasons behind the delay were the dispute over the delimitation of BMC
seats, and a legal battle over reservation for Other Backwards Classes
(OBC) in local body polls.

BMC Elections


Major changes after the election –

• BJP emerged as the dominant party in Maharashtra’s cities, with
Fadnavis leading its urban surge and outperforming rivals like
Congress, Shiv Sena (UBT), MNS, and NCP.

• For nearly 25 years (1997–2022), the undivided Shiv Sena
controlled BMC. These elections, however, mark a decisive end to
that era.

BMC Elections


• A major setback for the Pawar family as even the
temporary reunion of Ajit Pawar’s factions in Pune and Pimpri-
Chinchwad failed to yield electoral gains, leaving the BJP
unchallenged despite aggressive campaigning.

• Breaking from the MVA, Congress allied with Vanchit Bahujan
Aghadi and Rashtriya Samaj Paksh in Mumbai, but the move
delivered only modest results.

BMC Elections

Maharashtra State Election Commission (SEC) –

• The Maharashtra State Election Commission (SEC) is a
constitutional authority established under Article 243K of the
Constitution of India.

• It is responsible for conducting elections to local self-
government institutions in Maharashtra.

• The SEC has exclusive powers to supervise, direct, and control
elections to municipal corporations, municipal councils, and
panchayats, including the BMC.

BMC Elections


• It ensures free, fair, and transparent elections by issuing
schedules and enforcing the Model Code of Conduct.

• The Commission handles ward delimitation, electoral rolls,
and the polling and counting process.

• Though it uses state and local administrative machinery,
the SEC functions independently of the state government.

CEC of Maharashtra: Dinesh Waghmare

The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation was established in which
year?

A. 1865
B. 1872
C. 1888
D. 1909
ANSWER - C

The Mayor of Mumbai is elected by:

A. Direct election by citizens
B. Nomination by the Governor
C. Election from among elected corporators
D. Appointment by the Municipal Commissioner
ANSWER - C

The motion for impeachment of a Supreme Court judge must be
signed by at least:

A. 50 members of Lok Sabha or 25 members of Rajya Sabha
B. 100 members of Lok Sabha or 50 members of Rajya Sabha
C. 1/3rd members of either House
D. 2/3rd members of either House
ANSWER - B

Which of the following judges faced impeachment proceedings in
India, but was not removed?

A. Justice V. Ramaswami
B. Justice Soumitra Sen
C. Justice Dipak Misra
D. Justice J. Chelameswar
ANSWER - A

Which of the following correctly represents the composition of the
Inquiry Committee under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968?

A. Chief Justice of India, Attorney General, senior advocate
B. Supreme Court judge, Chief Justice of a High Court, eminent
jurist
C. Two MPs and one Supreme Court judge
D. Law Minister, senior judge, constitutional expert
ANSWER - B
